A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAE research framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoboTwin and ManiSkill evaluations, real-world manipulation experiments, and training and noise ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SIMPLER evaluations, bimanual and OOD real-world experiments, and additional analyses in Appendix F.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 introduces asynchronous VLM replanning, nearest-waypoint selection, directional filtering and spline merging into the executing trajectory. This adds closed-loop correction and failure recovery to the inference procedure. The underlying sparse geometric interface, diffusion expert and APPF training scheme remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds SIMPLER evaluation on Google Robot and WidowX tasks, four real-world bimanual tasks including towel folding and flower insertion, and held-out object-position scenarios. Appendix F adds C-Eval and CMMLU evaluations. The seven pretraining dataset sources and their 150k total trajectories are unchanged between v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 12.

E2.justification: The RoboTwin comparison adds π0-FAST and π0.5. The real-world comparison adds π0, π0-FAST, π0.5, SoFAR, HAMSTER and GR00T-N1 alongside retained baselines. New SIMPLER and trajectory-quality comparisons further expand comparator coverage, including Magma, HAMSTER and LLARVA in Table 18.

E3.justification: Reported real-world training changes from 50 to 20 demonstrations per task, with controlled ID/OOD positions and joint training for generalist baselines replacing v1's per-task baseline fine-tuning. New studies introduce depth-corruption, trajectory-quality and model-configuration protocols. GAE training duration changes from two plus three days to eight hours plus two days. The OOD allocation conflicts internally: Section 5.1 specifies four positions with five trials each, while Appendix C specifies five positions with four trials each.

E4.justification: v2 adds depth-noise robustness, interpolation, keyframe-selection, single-versus-multiple-benchmark fine-tuning, waypoint-density and backbone-size analyses, plus a failure-recovery case study. It supplements the retained APPF training curve with a quantitative comparison. Conversely, v1's point-cloud-source composition ablation and separate real-world MoGe/PromptDepth variants are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests or training-seed variability. The 20-trial real-world evaluation convention is retained, and v2's depth-noise study uses the same trial-count reporting approach without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive SIMPLER, bimanual/OOD and ablation results. Existing RoboTwin scores also change, such as Place A2B Left from 0.38 to 0.64, alongside revised camera-view and guidance-noise results; changed settings limit direct performance comparisons. The novel-color/object/instruction and ManiSkill scores from v1 Tables 4–5 remain in v2 Tables 14–15. Depth-source result entries disappear.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions for selecting the closest updated waypoint and enforcing forward directional consistency in closed-loop merging, Equations 1–2. The conditioning, diffusion and training-loss equations are retained with renumbering. No substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The central sparse-interface, reusable-expert and APPF claims remain. v2 removes the explicit first-attempt priority claim and promotes the existing 150k-trajectory dataset to a named contribution. Its abstract also clarifies that the expert remains frozen while the VLM receives lightweight fine-tuning, qualifying v1's broad zero-shot wording.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of IK failure under geometric errors and contact-rich conditions, interpretations of waypoint density and knowledge retention, and depth-noise failure boundaries. A new limitations section acknowledges the manually designed interface, depth-estimation costs and camera-calibration requirement. The earlier interpretation of mixed point-cloud sources reducing the simulation-to-real gap is removed with its ablation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Qwen2.5VL 7B, uncolored 512-point inputs, eight-step guidance/action chunks, learning rate, weight decay and 500/10 training/inference diffusion steps. It adds dual-arm teleoperation and task details, revises training durations, and promises future dataset release. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Appendix D names Adam, whereas Table 16 names AdamW.

R1.justification: v2 updates the literature with works including SoFAR, FAST, UniVLA, LLARVA and newer VLA research. It adds specific distinctions from HAMSTER and SoFAR and drops the first-attempt novelty claim. The overall positioning around geometric interfaces and reduced semantic burden remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial method explanations are rewritten, and the title and author information change. Experiments are reorganized into separate simulation, real-world and ablation sections. Data preparation and generalization material move into expanded appendices, with new limitations and impact sections replacing the earlier simpler structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns. The pipeline and task displays are redesigned, and new failure-recovery, position-grid and bimanual figures appear. Comparison tables gain baseline columns and ID-to-OOD entries, while numerous analysis tables are added. Existing generalization tables and demonstration sequences are also relocated or relabeled.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the reusable geometric expert through direct interface and depth-noise tests, broader real-world evaluation, clearer implementation details and explicit limitations. However, it removes source-composition evidence and introduces reporting problems: conflicting OOD protocols and RoboTwin averages inconsistent with displayed task scores, such as 0.82 versus a short-horizon mean of 0.8525 in Table 2. These defects limit confidence in the expanded evidence, leaving a supported but limited net quality improvement.
